newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland pledges crackdown on immigrants from east.
newsitem.headline: Poland pledges crackdown on immigrants from east.

text.p: Poland will tighten controls on its eastern border to stop illegal immigrants using the country as a transit route to the West, the new chief of the border guard said on Wednesday.

"We will do all we can to reduce the number of illegal immigrants. It is better to tighten the eastern border than to chase illegal immigrants inside the country," Andrzej Anklewicz told a news conference.

The government will employ 2,000 additional border guards this year, increase patrolling of its eastern borders and build new posts there, said Anklewicz, appointed to head the border guard under a recent reorganisation of the interior ministry.
He said a tight eastern border was crucial considering Poland's plans to join the European Union.
"At some point, when the date of our entry to the EU is known, it will become very clear that Poland cannot be a gateway for immigrants trying to make it to the common Europe," he said.
He said guards had caught about 15,000 illegal immigrants annually during the last three years and 11,000 people were returned to Poland last year after unsuccessful attempts to enter Germany.
Because of liberal border regulations it is difficult to estimate how many illegal immigrants Poland hosts, but some analysts say their number could be as high as 200,000.
Most of them enter from the eastern border with Russia, Ukraine, Lithuania and Belarus, smuggled in by professional guides in cars, lorries and planes or on foot.
Last year the police made several spectacular arrests of organised groups of illegal immigrants heading for Germany.
In a recent case, border guards in the south-western province of Zielona Gora near Germany detained a group of 103 illegal immigrants from 10 countries, most of them Asians and Africans.
